卡瓦基紐的刷弦型是整個合奏的律動基礎，旋律手會依照它決定句子長度與重音位置。它不: The cavaquinho's strumming pattern is the rhythmic foundation of the whole ensemble, and the melody players decide the length of their phrases and the placing of their accents from it. It is not background but one of the organisers of time and groove.
卡瓦基紐的角色特別容易被誤解。它是一種小型的四弦吉他，音域較高，刷弦的方式有固定: The cavaquinho's role is especially easy to misread. It is a small four-string guitar, higher in range, and its strumming follows fixed patterns (levadas), each pattern matching one rhythmic groove. These patterns are not casual accompaniment but the groove foundation of the whole ensemble: the melody players decide the length of their phrases and the placing of their accents from the cavaquinho's pattern. So the cavaquinho is not a supporting player; it is one of the organisers of time and groove.
另一個常被忽略的層次是「誰在什麼時候可以加裝飾」。紹羅的裝飾音不是毫無節制地疊加: Another layer that is often overlooked is who may add ornaments when. Choro's ornaments are not piled on without restraint: the main melody and the bandolim often play their own ornamental lines at the same time, using differences of range and rhythm to avoid covering each other; when one is dense with ornaments the other often thins to simpler lines or long notes so that the detail shows through. This instinct for making room is why choro sounds dense without being messy. It rests not on fixed rules worked out in rehearsal but on the judgement of each performance.
另一支旋律樂器（曼陀林、薩克斯風或單簧管）: A second melody instrument (bandolim, saxophone or clarinet)
合奏靠什麼協調？答案是「聽潘德羅與卡瓦基紐的節奏型，旋律手之間以樂句呼吸互相提示: What holds the ensemble together? The answer is: listen to the rhythmic patterns of the pandeiro and the cavaquinho, and let the melody players cue each other through the breathing of their phrases. Choro has no conductor, and the change from one section to the next is usually signalled by a melody player with a clear phrase: before entering the second part, the main melody closes its sentence in a way that can be anticipated, and the other players hear that closing and know the section is turning. The signal is not a gesture but part of the music itself. Because of this, choro players have to know the whole shape of the piece and cannot memorise only their own line; a player who does not know it, however good, will miss the beat at the turn.
和爵士小編制的差別在聲部的關係。爵士小編制分成節奏組與前線，前線輪流獨奏，節奏組: The difference from a jazz combo is the relation between the parts. A jazz combo divides into a rhythm section and a front line, the front line solos in turn and the rhythm section supplies harmony and time; choro has no such layering — every instrument weaves counterpoint on the same timeline, and the guitar's inner parts are often an independent melodic line too.
巴西紹羅（Choro）— 以長笛或薩克斯風、曼陀林、卡瓦基紐與吉他交織對位的巴西: Choro — a Brazilian chamber ensemble tradition in which flute or saxophone, mandolin, cavaquinho and guitar weave counterpoint. Ensembles and instrumentation by Next Door Sound Weavers.
常被拿來對比的是薩爾薩樂團。兩者都靠一個反覆的節奏型組織全團，也都沒有指揮；但薩: The common comparison is the salsa band. Both organise the whole group around a repeating rhythmic pattern and both have no conductor; but salsa's shared reference is the clave, a two-bar cycle that every part's accents align to, whereas choro has no single, rigid two-bar cycle of that kind: its rhythmic skeleton is made by the cavaquinho's levada together with the pandeiro's patterns, and the coordination also rests on the melody players closing their phrases in a predictable way at section changes. One shares a single map of time, the other relies on the interlocking of phrase with phrase.
提供低音線、內聲部與和聲的基礎；七弦吉他常負責低音: Supplies the bass line, the inner parts and the harmonic foundation; the seven-string guitar often takes the bass
曲目上，紹羅有華爾滋（valsa）、抒情歌曲（choro-canção）、馬克西: In repertoire choro has several types — the valsa (waltz), the choro-canção (lyric song), the maxixe — with different rhythms and tempos. What they share is melody in front, counterpoint woven underneath, ornaments densely applied: on the same piece different players add different ornaments, so no two performances are quite the same.
比較不同樂團演奏同一首曲子的版本：裝飾音與對位方式通常都不一樣。: Compare recordings of the same piece by different groups: the ornaments and the counterpoint are usually different.
注意潘德羅的重音如何隨著旋律的句子改變。: Notice how the pandeiro's accents change with the phrasing of the melody.
注意長笛與曼陀林什麼時候交錯、什麼時候同向。對位不是和聲，兩條線各自獨立。: Notice when the flute and the mandolin cross and when they move in the same direction. Counterpoint is not harmony; the two lines are independent.
演奏主題，加上裝飾音、顫音與快速的音階裝飾；兩者常輪流或同時擔任主旋律: Plays the theme with ornaments, trills and fast scale decoration; the two often take the main melody in turn or at the same time
紹羅就是巴西的森巴，只是用不同的樂器演奏。: Choro is just Brazilian samba played on different instruments.
紹羅成形於里約熱內盧的街頭與室內聚會，早年常在家庭、酒吧、咖啡館與慶典中演奏。它: Choro took shape in the streets and the indoor gatherings of Rio de Janeiro, and in its early years was played in homes, bars, cafés and celebrations. It is a social music: the players sit around together, take turns on the theme and on solos, and the audience listens from close by. Later it moved into concert halls and studios, but its chamber, small-scale nature did not change.
紹羅是室內器樂合奏，強調旋律的對位與裝飾；森巴是集體的打擊樂傳統，強調節奏的層次: Choro is a chamber instrumental ensemble stressing contrapuntal melody and ornament; samba is a collective percussion tradition stressing layers of rhythm and groove. They share Rio's urban setting and part of their rhythmic vocabulary, but the line-up, the occasions and the musical logic are all different.
紹羅的卡瓦基紐只是伴奏樂器，負責刷和弦。: Choro's cavaquinho is just an accompaniment instrument that strums the chords.
紹羅的核心技術是對位（contraponto），而不是「和弦加旋律」。在一般的流: Choro's core technique is counterpoint (contraponto), not chords plus a melody. In ordinary pop music the melody is on top and the chords underneath, a vertical relation; in choro two or three melodic lines run at once, independent of each other and answering each other, a horizontal relation. The flute blows one phrase and the mandolin plays another at the same point in time; they need not share notes or rhythm, but together they make a complete harmony. These basic contrapuntal lines are usually written by the arranger, and what the players add in performance is ornaments and small interactions.
紹羅的核心是對位：每一條線都要聽到別人在做什麼，才能即時調整自己的句子。這是一種: Choro's core is counterpoint: every line has to hear what the others are doing in order to adjust its own sentence on the spot. It is a technique of listening to each other, not the sum of each playing well.
紹羅的樂手各自演奏自己的部分，合起來就會好聽。: Choro players each play their own part and it sounds good when put together.
紹羅的編制不是分成「旋律」與「伴奏」兩層，而是每一件樂器都在同一條時間線上編織。: Choro's line-up is not divided into a melody layer and an accompaniment layer; every instrument weaves on the same timeline. The most common combination has the flute or the bandolim taking the main melody in turn or together, the cavaquinho turning the harmony into rhythm, the guitar (violão) supplying bass and inner parts, and the pandeiro keeping the overall groove.
紹羅與森巴（samba）的關係很深，但兩者不是同一件事。紹羅的節奏較為輕快、連續: Choro and samba are closely related but not the same thing. Choro's rhythm is lighter and more continuous, stressing melodic ornament and counterpoint; samba's rhythm is heavier, stressing layers of percussion and collective groove. The two influenced each other historically, but a choro ensemble is usually smaller, more chamber-like and more dependent on the skill of individual players. The relation can be put in one sentence: choro is Rio's chamber instrumental tradition, samba is Rio's collective festival tradition; they share one city and part of their rhythmic vocabulary, but they solve different problems.
紹羅（choro）是十九世紀在里約熱內盧成形的一種器樂合奏傳統，以旋律樂器、撥弦: Choro is an instrumental ensemble tradition that took shape in Rio de Janeiro in the nineteenth century, a small band of melody instruments, plucked strings and percussion playing pieces that are fast, heavily ornamented and woven part against part. The problem it has to solve is a little like the jazz combo's: with no conductor, relying mainly on listening and word-of-mouth understanding, let several parts improvise and interact at once; and its answer is not a rhythm section plus a front line but every instrument in counterpoint.
結構上，紹羅的曲子通常有三個或更多部分（primeira、segunda、ter: In structure, a choro piece usually has three or more parts (primeira, segunda, terceira parte), played in order and often each repeated, making a multi-section form such as AABBCC or ABABCC; some pieces bring the theme back between contrasting sections. This form lets the players add different ornaments and counterpoint on each repeat. The tempo is usually fast and the ornaments dense, and the players must keep every note clear inside a quick rhythm. This fast but not messy quality is the hardest thing in choro.
維持整體的律動，以搖晃、拇指與指尖製造細分的聲響: Keeps the overall groove, making subdivided sounds with the shake, the thumb and the fingertips
聽吉他的內聲部：它不是只有低音，常常有一條隱藏的旋律線。: Listen to the guitar's inner parts: it is not only bass, there is often a hidden melodic line.
與主旋律交織成對位，提供另一條獨立的線條: Weaves counterpoint with the main melody, supplying another independent line
與藍草樂隊的差別在誰負責時間。藍草不用鼓，拍子由曼陀林第二、四拍的 chop 與: The difference from a bluegrass band is who is responsible for time. Bluegrass uses no drums; the beat is made by the mandolin's chop on beats two and four together with the double bass on beats one and three, and during solos the others fall back to a fixed rhythmic net. Choro has the pandeiro, the groove is kept by the hand drum and the cavaquinho together, and the accompanists keep their groove patterns but add contrapuntal ornaments and changes of accent.
調音與記譜方面，紹羅的樂器音域差異很大：長笛在高音，曼陀林與卡瓦基紐在中高音，吉: In tuning and notation, choro's instruments differ widely in range: the flute is high, the bandolim and cavaquinho in the upper middle, the guitar in the lower middle. The arranger has to give each of them a place in the same harmony rather than crowding them all together. Because the ranges are so far apart, a choro ensemble sounds clearly layered: high melody and counterpoint, middle harmonic rhythm, low roots and inner parts, all three running at once.
這套編制的關鍵在於「沒有純伴奏」。卡瓦基紐看起來像伴奏，但它刷的和弦型本身有固定: The key to this line-up is that there is no pure accompaniment. The cavaquinho looks like accompaniment, but the chord patterns it strums have their own rhythmic logic and interlock with the melody; the guitar looks like the bass, but its inner parts are often an independent melodic line; the pandeiro looks like a metronome, but its accents change with the phrasing of the melody. Every instrument is on the same timeline, which is why choro sounds dense.
